definition.en: The right and real possibility of every person to turn to the courts and to other dispute-resolution mechanisms, and to participate in them effectively and on an equal basis, whether as a party, witness, victim or in any other capacity.

en: It is not exhausted by formal judicial protection: it requires removing the economic, physical, communication and attitudinal barriers that impede it. For persons with disabilities, the CRPD guarantees it in art. 13, which requires procedural accommodations that are age- and gender-appropriate, accessibility and training for those working in the administration of justice; unlike reasonable accommodation, procedural accommodations are not subject to the disproportionate-burden limit. It also has a gender dimension – justice free from stereotypes for women victims of violence – and a childhood dimension – child-friendly justice for children and adolescents.

prefLabel.en: Rights, legal capacity and access to justice
